column1: # Standalone-inference rows that do NOT work on the pinned toolchain, and why.
# Read by the "Assert standalone inference results" step. Any row not listed here must pass, with
# the backend it resolved and a real execution_path both asserted. A row listed here must FAIL, and
# fail with the named cause — if it starts passing, or fails for a different reason, the job goes
# red and says so. These are recorded limitations, not silenced ones.
# Toolchain: TornadoVM v6.0.0, which pom.xml declares (tornadovm.base.version), built from its tag
# by .github/actions/setup-tornadovm.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   backend  model  quantization  configuration  cause-substring
# TornadoVM 6.0.0 removed the former batch-prefill and hidden-class failures.
# Phi-3 FP16 is numerically correct on an M4 Pro: CPU/Metal parity has zero violations across
# 2,052,096 logits (max absolute difference 0.0029875), and legacy/lowered parity passes.
# Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 F16 no longer fits the free memory on the Linux runner. Its working
# set measures 14980 MiB peak (nvidia-smi sampled through a full run, -n 160, --gpu-memory 14GB)
# against an RTX 5070 Ti holding 15.5 GB with the driver already in it -- under 7% headroom.
# It used to fit, and no commit changed that. Run 34582487450 on main passed this row on
# 2026-09-11; re-running that same job from that same commit on that same runner on 2026-09-16
# failed it, at the same 112 MiB allocation, with 21 of the 22 rows otherwise identical. The
# runner lost roughly a gigabyte of free memory between those dates. CUDA fails the allocation
# outright, OpenCL fails it asynchronously once per queued command.
# The fix belongs on the runner, not here. These lines keep the job reporting the one row that
# is broken, and a NEW PASS turns it red the day the memory comes back, which is the signal to
# delete them. Every other Mistral row, Q8_0 included, still has to pass.
cuda
opencl
